A fundraising event in Toronto and an opinion piece on lessons from the quake for the Dominican Republic also emerged.

logs.summary: A powerful magnitude 7.6–7.7 earthquake struck southern Panama on October 9, 2026, with its epicenter near Pitaloza Arriba in Herrera province. The quake triggered tsunami warnings for multiple countries across Central and South America, prompted evacuations and building shakes in Panama City, and caused some damage, though the Panama Canal was not affected. Initial USGS estimates of 8.0 were downgraded, and aftershocks were reported.

logs.summary:
On October 25, 2026, a powerful earthquake struck near Japan's Bonin Islands (Ogasawara Islands) in the Pacific Ocean, with preliminary magnitudes reported between 6.3 and 7.0. The Japan Meteorological Agency stated no tsunami warnings were issued. The quake was attributed to tectonic plate movements along the Pacific "Ring of Fire."
A deep earthquake struck near Japan's Bonin Islands on October 25, with magnitudes reported between 6.5 and 7.0 and a depth of approximately 470–500 km. The tremor was felt over a wide area from the Kanto region to Tohoku, including Tokyo, but no tsunami warning was issued, and there was no tsunami threat to Hawaii.

logs.summary: A magnitude 5.6 earthquake struck off the coast of Guatemala near Puerto San José on November 10, 2026, causing buildings to shake in Guatemala City and being felt in neighboring El Salvador and Nicaragua. No immediate reports of damage or casualties were mentioned in the initial coverage.

logs.summary: Additional reports from November 10-11 provide more precise details on the magnitude 5.6-5.8 earthquake off Guatemala's coast, including a depth of 35 km and epicenter 43 km south of Puerto San Jose. The tremor was felt across Guatemala, El Salvador, and Nicaragua, with no casualties or damage reported.

news.headline: 5.6-Magnitude Earthquake Strikes off Coast of Guatemala
news.body: Guatemala City, November 11 (QNA) â€“ The United States Geological Survey (USGS) reported that a 5.6-magnitude earthquake struck off the coast of Guatemala, causing buildings in the capital to shake. There have been no immediate reports of injuries or damage resulting from the earthquake. The USGS stated that the earthquake occurred 43 kilometers south of the coastal town of Puerto San Jose, at a depth of 35 kilometers. The tremor was also felt by residents in El Salvador and Nicaragua; both countries indicated that there is no risk of a tsunami. On September 16, a 5.3-magnitude earthquake struck southern Guatemala. Guatemala is located over an active geological zone, which frequently triggers strong earthquakes across Central American and the Caribbean. (QNA)
